requirements.note: All contacts sorted by last name (Abbott, Abbott, Abbott, Adeyemi…), lettered sections with pinned headers, and a working A–Z index (with a ★ entry) that jumps to the right letter.

Filters live by company ('willow'), phone ('389-8378'), email and name. The clear button and Close restore the full list, and the index shrinks to only the letters that match. A 'No Results for …' empty state shows.
Details show avatar, name, company, Call/Email buttons, tinted phone and email rows with ↗ affordances, and the birthday when known (hidden when absent).
Add/Remove from Favorites on details. Favorites show as a horizontal avatar strip at the top of the list with a count, and a star appears on the row. Persists.
Add/Edit sheet with labelled fields. Save is disabled for blank or whitespace-only names and when both names are cleared during edit. Return moves to the next field, and input is trimmed on save.
Swipe-to-delete on rows and a Delete Contact button on details, both with a confirmation.
Favorite, edit and deletions survived relaunch, and the search text is not wrongly restored.

bugs: Delete-contact confirmation popover on the details screen is anchored to the top of the screen, pointing at the name, not at the Delete button the user tapped.
tells: Swipe-to-delete action is teal (app tint) instead of the system destructive red.
The main list opens with the large title already collapsed to an inline 'Contacts'; the large title only appears when you pull down.
About 60pt of empty white space under the favorites carousel before the 'A' section.
At the largest text size the section index overlaps the favorites carousel, cutting off names ('Fel… Adey…'), and the carousel avatars stay small while the names are huge.
Strong custom teal/mint branding (gradient initials avatars, tinted Call/Email pills): polished, but more styled than a stock iOS app.
In the add form the live avatar preview shows only 'Q' when the first name has leading spaces.
A.scroll: Smooth with no blank rows or pop-in. Section headers pin with a blur under the nav bar, flings carry good momentum, pull-past-top bounces and reveals the large title, and scroll position is kept when returning from details.

requirements.note: Sorted by last name with letter sections and a blue system-style A–Z index (with ★) that jumps correctly. Section headers do not stay pinned, so after a jump or scroll the current letter is not visible.
Bottom search bar filters by company, phone (formatted or digits only), email and name. The clear button and the 'Clear Search' empty-state button restore the list.
Stock-Contacts-like details: avatar, name, company, blue phone and email links, birthday. No Call/Email quick-action buttons.
Add/Remove from Favorites with a star. Favorites form a plain section at the top of the list. Persists.
New/Edit Contact sheet. Done is disabled for empty or whitespace-only names, with a hint. Names are trimmed and edits apply.
Swipe-to-delete on rows (red 'Delete Contact', deletes immediately) and Delete Contact on details with an alert.
Favorite, add/edit and deletions survived relaunch.

bugs: The search query persists across relaunch: the app reopened with the old query, the list said 'No Contacts Found' and the title subtitle read '0 contacts', which looks like the directory is empty.
When a row is swiped open for delete, its name disappears; only the chevron is left on a grey pill.
tells: The large title never collapses on scroll: 'Contacts' plus the count stay fixed at full size and the list is hard-clipped beneath them, with no scroll-edge effect.
The list stops above the bottom search bar instead of scrolling under it.
Section headers are not sticky: grey full-width bands scroll away, unlike a plain UITableView or List.
Section header bands have a web-like look: flat grey full-width bars with extra spacing, especially in search results.
Fling momentum feels lighter than a native list: repeated hard flings cover fewer rows than expected.
B.scroll: No blank rows or pop-in and position is kept on return, but the fixed large header with hard clipping, non-sticky section headers and slightly short fling momentum make it feel less like a native iPhone list.

why: Both meet every requirement, but A's list behaves like a real iOS list: pinned section headers, a collapsing large title, content scrolling under the bars, and smooth momentum. Its details screen and forms are more finished. B looks closer to stock Contacts at a glance, but its frozen header, non-sticky sections, swipe row that loses its label, and search query restored on relaunch ('0 contacts') feel less like a native app; A's flaws are mostly cosmetic (teal swipe action, misplaced popover, carousel gap).
